comment: Nice hike overall, views of the falls are very mediocre but still a nice view to reward yourself with roughly halfway through. Nice balance of incline and flat elevation. Bathrooms in the parking lot are somewhat clean. Not messy but lots of flies… so that was a no for me. Lots of grasshoppers and butterflies!

This was a solid, challenging hike. A good amount of elevation gain and well maintained/well marked trail. Entering the park is a little annoying if you don’t pre-pay, but there is plenty of parking and it’s a really good weekend workout. It took us about 2 hours with a few toddler-related slowdowns.
Great views but very very buggy. Bug spray is essential
Nice walk, lots of wild flowers. Some of the old path is closed, near the waterfall, which is a shame. No water tap at the parking, hole in the ground toilets.

View was ok
Bring water as there’s no fountain available

Well-marked trail and was pretty quick, took us about 35 mins to get to the falls. Decent incline on the way back with some slippery sections, but not bad when you go at a slow and steady pace. Also not too buggy for mid-June!

Trails are well marked, parking is easy and there are washrooms available at the trail head. Multiple loop options but this time of year it’s a blend of icey and muddy trail conditions, bring your crampons and your fall waterproof boots — especially if you’re going deeper into the park
Great afternoon hike
Beautiful scenery and falls, although area close to falls has been closed off. Although beware; snow is deep off the trail path!
Not so scenic in the winter, the trails are well maintained!
Very pretty and well marked/maintained!
It's well maintained.
Steep trails! Good if you have a hiking stick
great trail - from parking lot to falls and back it was steeper than what we expected based on trail reviews - not stroller friendly

Very nice trail but it’s HARD, I only did half of what I wanted. It was supposed to be 2-3hrs to do the whole loop but it would’ve been 3-5hrs had I done it. Going to the waterfall and back to the parking lot took me 2hrs to do 6km. It’s a very hard and very steep hike for a lot of it.
Nice trail, steep when coming back from the waterfall
Was amazing
Some elevation changes, a waterfall at the end, apple trees, wildflowers, caterpillars, chipmunks, a garter snake, and fall colours!
The elevation is not child's play on the way to the falls. The wild flower meadows are great... And the vista at the bottom of the trail before the falls trail is the real show stopper
Trail was moderate with a falls view at the end. Weather was super conventional for the hike. Overall, it was awesome!
Road closed signs shouls be ignored to get to park
Beautiful trail lots of fun, trail is closed off a a certain point which was the only downside to it but solid hike and washrooms are available about halfway through.
Too many bugs flying in summer time
Seemed too difficult to be a moderate. Also the falls were closed when we got there
The original loop itself is moderate, it doesn’t really have any shade so early mornings or late afternoons would be best. The falls hike I wouldn’t say was moderate and was actually pretty difficult
It was a nice hike. A bit climbing but it wasn't too difficult. The official view point in the waterfall is closed due to safety issues so you can the them fron the path.

Great for hiking enthusiasts, nature lovers and anyone into a bit of adventure. The trail has some ups and downs but nothing too tough. Just don’t expect an amazing view at the top, it’s not that impressive.
Love it
Overall park was really nice, the trails were well maintained. Some of the signage was missing or confusing plus there were some trail closures but it was a great hike.

The trail was really amazing and cold winds made a much more easier hike. 
While coming back we were lucky to see a deer in the wild. 

Overall well maintained trails !
Cool waterfall, pretty uphill, but not too challenging if you take your time
Great trail, well marked with beautiful views. Mixed terrain with wet conditions towards the falls, some steps/elevation included as well.
Good hike to falls
Some areas a bit steep so bring your hiking shoes.
Very steep at points!
Great great trail. Come here every season. Bring a camera and capture some of the beauty.
Good trail the river was nice. The falls was  harder to see and not as nice.

The trail had a lot of fluffy snow which was packed down enough to be passable without being icy. The hills get your heart pumping and we had to take water breaks on some of the longer ones. The views are nice (though the falls themselves were underwhelming). Felt like a good workout.
Paid parking to let yall know about 10-20$
Great easy to moderate trail, nice views, decent elevation gain, very well maintained. In the middle of November not crowded especially in the morning.
Great trail! Some pretty steep spots so just be prepared for a good incline!
Pleasant fall hike though trees mostly bare.  Walk to falls very pretty.  Tree blocking trail, fairly easy to climb over
turkeys !!!! leaves!! waterfall !!!

Went early in the morning, it was a straightforward hike ending with the falls. It might be difficult if the ground is wet or muddy, especially going down in certain places. To enter the area you do require a day-use permit.
Great colours
Beginner friendly trails - well marked. Beautiful views of fall foliage

Beautiful trail and very clean. Options of taking trails that are more difficult if you’re feeling like doing that…many choices. Not overcrowded and lots of parking . Will definitely be back and would absolutely recommend.
Beautiful trail and gorgeous scenery!
Beautiful trail and gorgeous scenery!
Nice trail and well maintained. However, very annoyed I had to pay for parking , only to park in basically a field
Good hike
Bit of a spooky decent to the base of the waterfall but totally doable - just take your time
Bring water -nowhere to fill up. Book reservation online - you need this to get in the gate.

Highly recommended!
One of the best trails in this region

Good cardio with big rewards.  My girls have agreed to come with me again, provided that snacks are provided next time.  Seriously do bring extra water and snacks.  We built up a good sweat. 

No mosquitoes at this time.  Conditions were excellent.
A little overgrown in places but overall very nice
lots of hills, some are pretty steep and long
The trail is nice, most of it in the sun with no shade. The main attraction is the view point of the waterfall,  and the current point of view is not the best.
Not what I was expecting, but not disappointing in the least.

Combination of grasslands and forest. Trail packed solid surface, steps, rocks, roots - hiking boots highly recommended..
Cataract falls at the end of out-and-back portion of the Bruce Trail is beautiful even though view partially obstructed by vegetation..
Bring bug spray and a water!
The trail needs a bit of nature clearing. It is on the trail on some parts
Well marked. Clear path. Great trail for families.
Enjoyed the trail, nice views .. only downfall was the access to  view the falls was closer was closed. Only able to view it from a far distance.
Trail was beautiful, for people who are planning to go towards the Cataract falls it’s a very poor view from the trail.
Strenuous hike to a beautiful waterfall
Around 30% shaded, great hike with some nice sections of incline and decline. The view of the falls is not too bad either.
30% shaded. Beautiful trail with lots of wildlife but spoiled by recent acts of vandalism. Shame!
Beautiful trails, some good inclines along the way, mix of open fields/meadow and forest. It wasn’t busy so had some nice open and quiet space. Would recommend!
meadow, forest, and falls!! the lookout area is closed off but you can get around. lots of shade and sunny parts perfect for early summer
Pay to access trail
Could be steep at parts for some.  Worth the trek!  Beautiful scenery. Saw a  painted turtle, snapping turtle, birds, butterflies!  Lilac trees were in full bloom.  Great hike!

Right now there are lots of mosquitoes, we got bit quite a bit. 
Really nice trail moderately rough.
Picnic benches available 
Washrooms available 
Some areas of the trail are stroller friendly but it is a dirt road so you would need a stroller that can withstand these types of roads
It’s a bit muddy, otherwise a great trail. Gets a bit challenging climbing the hills but that’s part of the fun.
Muddy in some spots but very nice. Must be gorgeous in the spring and summer. Looking forward to some of the closed trails reopening.
Beautiful day on the trail. Not muddy at all. Took a different route than we usually do today and discovered some bridges and water.
Not my favourite hike but it was plan B
Snowshoes are recommended. It's perfect out!

Icy trail and lots of uphill and downhill on this day. 
 But it was funny or fun. Lol. Walking stick helped.

A little icy up the steep incline section of the trail, as well as near the ruins by the river. Overall, it was a nice experience with the recent snow. The park installed new automatic gates right at the entrance off the road, which caused a bit of a traffic jam at the entrance.
Great walk, some steep uphill and downhill. A little icy in the winter. A few different side trails options that loop back into the main one. Nice views of the waterfall from the bridges.
The vibes were just… so immaculate. The haze, the sound of the water, the light snow… gave me a feeling I’ve never had before.
Trails a little muddy. And there is construction work by the falls.
Fun little challenging

The path to the falls outlook is steep with huge steps down, lots of leaves and rocks on the ground, challenging with little elevation. Not so much of good views, very open, no tall trees surrounding for most parts of the trail, super windy today.
meadow trail near the falls was closed but you could still see the falls from another point

A little slick because of rain

Good elevation.
Saw my favourite view of the park during this hike. Will have to return each year to see the beautiful view

Weak wifi

Its got everything
Well marked for directions. Lots of people as expected. Beautiful meadows.
rocky and wet in places
A lot of elevation for a not very satisfying view of the waterfall
Love this one. There’s a fair amount of changes in elevation and the waterfall is a nice treat too!
the trail is in good shape. Some exposed stone and erosion of trail, pay attention around steep sections.
A long average hike to get to the creek, once there is nicer but the waterfall is not so good. Loop is blocked off.
Busy, it's a walk in the field. Viewing platform non existant. Wouldn't be back

Bring lots of water. So uphill
 climbing if you go to the falls.
Easy trail, can’t really see the falls due to construction.
Muddy,but to be expected. Part of trail looks like they are clear cutting, no trees left. The only good part is when you reach the falls.

Very icy and/or muddy in sections, still quite a bit of snow. The trail is rugged and use of walking sticks is highly recommended!

Trans Canada Trail was very water logged!  Made it very challenging.  The rest of the trails were more snowy.  

The Bruce trail to the waterfall was classic Bruce trail…. Nice and challenging up and down hills.  

When you first see the waterfalls take your photos.  When you get to the end of the trail you are more ‘on top of the waterfall’ and not as great photos.

We took the challenge of the side trail to climb up the hill to save some mileage of walking around.  Was worth the challenge!  We’re we’re slipping and sliding some but taught my 3 kids to dig deep and endure and persevere.  Even is adults were sliding back some.  Made lots of memories and I’m sure we will talk about the ‘time we climbed the snowy hill’
So much snow!!!!! We literally had to make the path lol beautiful day but Snowshoes would have been nice.
Too muddy; construction equipment cutting down trees in fields diminishes experience.
Trail alternates packed and loose snow so some sections are more strenuous. No ice today.
All stairs covered under snow, not easy trail, and waterfall view point disappointed a little. But we enjoyed it. Actually I suggest everyone paying for parking, cause fine is 30cad
YOU HAVE TO MAKE A RESERVATION IN ADVANCE THEY WILL TICKET YOU $30
Extremely icy. No hand rails on steep inclines. Very slippery so be careful. Waterfall was nice but a little far to see.
Slippery when wet. Blood and tears were created.
Nice little trail, only one other car in the lot today.
Meadow is muddy with the warmer weather but what a beautiful park. Love this place and coming back in the spring with a fishing rod.
Great Place! Very nice trail!
Was nice to see this trail again this year!
Come prepared for a good walk. Great views very hilly bring water and shoes. It’s a real hike but well worth it.
Tiring but beautiful
Climbed a big hill
Quite a long open section before you get to the woods and a river. Waterfall is average, concrete sides and not the best view. Very busy during fall season book before.
Some steep uphill stretch
Nice walk with various types of trails.  Too bad the viewing platform is closed.
Nice falls
Hike to the Cataract Falls Lookout is slightly challenging but feels great.

It was a really great day today. Temperature was nice and a good breeze. This trail really got my heart going with the inclines. We went down that very long staircase to see the rapids and river. There are between 200 to 300 steps each way! I stopped counting after 150. It's definitely a trail I'm glad I did.
The photos are VERY MISLEADING!! Cant see the waterfall if you follow this trail! Only from a very far distance and the waterfall is also obstructed by trees
Easy going down, coming back up was more difficult
It was dry after all the wet weather. The ground ranges from soil to stones to roots to sand depending on which trail you take and where you go.  My 4 teenage boys loved it.
Technically it’s not a fall, but the trail is great!
Nice trail with a few steep inclines. The views of the waterfall are quite obstructed.
Very hot in the late afternoon. Would recommend to wait and go in the evening especially if you have a dog.
Lame waterfall
Great but half of it is closed by the falls wont loop around
Beautiful river view
Nice walk. Not too difficult but good up hills. View from the top is not great but along the river is nice
Good trail but be aware that the road from McLaren Road to the main parking lot is full of potholes.
Omg so many uphills and with my baby on my back I almost cried. Was beautiful.
Muddy, falls entrance is barricaded so only from a distance

it's beautiful and well marked. 
easy one!
Pretty! Very hilly
It was such a beautiful hike! Went in February of 2022 and the snow on the trees and on the waterfall were amazing. I definitely recommend this trail!
Steep parts. You have to back track when going to the falls quite challenging in winter

The trail was snow covered which was very pretty.
A little icy in some places but beautiful.
The elevation fluctuates quite a bit but should be doable for most people.
Reserve ahead!
We paid for our park visit with a borrowed commercial vehicle park’s pass from my local library - awesome program to help everyone see our beautiful parks!
currently very icy, otherwise it's a great trail and quite scenic.

This was an okay trail. It was definitely easy for a seasoned hiker but offered lots of nice scenery. The waterfall isn’t worth the journey here, if that’s what you’re looking for. It’s lovely first thing in the morning. Since this is a provincial park, be sure to buy a reservation or day pass to access the area. I once made the mistake of coming here without doing so and was turned away. Overall, this is a relaxed hike with a few inclines to get your heart racing every so often.

Wide, well groomed, easy to follow trail. The two big hills are no joke! The falls view is very disappointing. To avoid people going over the awful barrier, it would be smart to close the trail and build a better lookout! I used the online reservation system, but there was also a machine to pay there.
nice hike, decent vertical, well marked, crosses, intersects with Bruce Trail
Little muddy, that hill is pretty intense but if you take your time it’s totally doable. If you have trekking poles, bring Em!
Nice hike. The steep ridge is pretty tiring but still great. Would love if the trail was fixed at the falls.

Nice trail, well groomed. We avoided the steep hills leading to the water falls by taking side trails. There is a side trail that runs parallel to the trail leading to the falls and you return to the car park via the trail way. This makes for a nice loop of 4.6k total. Some day we will do the falls trail as well.
Great trail. But too many people and lotsa them with no trail etiquette. Saw two families litter and throw food and plastic near the beach. Hope they start fining for this
Hills
It’s a nice trail. Beware of 2 heavy climbs.
Trail is cut off at the falls…other then that, it’s a good trail.
Good workout. Lots of hills. The falls are anti-climatic, you can’t get close but still, a good energizing hike.
Beat hiking trail ever
If you are looking for a hike, this is a HIKE!
Lots of uphill but my 10 yo made it with only minor complaints. About 7k there and back.

Serious elevations and nice variety. we had to book our slot at ontario parks website
no gate but on the weekends there are guards asking for the booking. parking used to be by machine but that's closed now.
waterfall is closed off too, you can just view it.
Town blocked all road parking so only parking was in the park, preregister for $7.50. Navigation takes you to parking on the road.  Good hike but pretty crowded
Great hike. Big path. We did it when it was very very hot and the climbs were okay, but the path without the sun was hot

Nice hike on a well maintained trail. Steep hills, but easy to navigate on foot. Lots of butterflies, and surprisingly no biting bugs. Part of the trail is closed, so it's an in & out to the falls rather than a loop.

The trail was okay, quite a bit of bugs. The view of the falls is only from a distance, you can't get too close to it. 

The elevation is exhausting but good practice for larger hikes!
During this time, the loop is closed. The trail ends at the falls view
Picked up a lot of garbage on the hike. Didn't get a good view of the falls due to trail closures. Didn't have to pay for parking.
Awesome falls view where the trail ends
was a little disappointed in the trail

Well maintained trail, it has washrooms , unfortunately the access to the falls is closed. As you get closer to the falls the walk gets challenging. $7.50 for parking, now you can book online on Ontario Parks website

Beautiful views, however very little shade cover and far walks between water sources. We were followed by horse flies the entire time despite having deep woods bug spray, so come prepared
Lots of birds. The trail to the falls was probably not worth the hike.
Amazing
Just okay, nothing spectacular. View of the falls is mostly blocked by trees.
We did this trail in March - varied terrain and views. Part of the trail was blocked off so we viewed the falls from farther away rather than exploring them up close.
Its good for a hike we had fun and my dogs love the hike. If you are coming just to see the falls its not really worth it. You can barely see them.

Very well maintained and lots of signage. 
Does get quite busy I went early and but the time I left the parking lot was full.
Nice day easy trail. Always good for a nice long walk.
Really busy when I went
Due to COVID they restrict number of visitors. We got lucky but saw ppl walking along the road for a kilometre to get to the park. Also parking is paid. Trail and falls are just fine
Excellent view of waterfall, muddy is quite a few spots still.
Beautiful scenery throughout trail.
super icy!
Great out and back hike to the falls. Conditions on trail to falls pretty treacherous due to ice. Crampons were a must.
Very icy
Beautiful walk

Spectacular. Getting to the falls is kinda dangerous/illegal-ish, so be careful. But going behind the falls is unnnnnnbelievable! The "parking lot was full" when I got there, so I started from a cataract trail off a side street.
Beautiful out there. But lots of snow today and it wasn’t easy out there in hiking boots. I managed but would have preferred snowshoes.
Great in Winter

Great quick little hike with hills, Jan 17 2021 was VERY ICEY. We didn't have traction aids on our boots and, as a group of 3 in our mid-late 20s, had a hilarious time clambering on all 4s and sliding down hills. If you want to stay up right you'll need additions to your boots! Get there early (we got there at 9AM) to avoid crowds, by the time we left (noon-ish) the trail was busy and the car park full- can confirm when we left parking tickets were being checked
A bit slippery on the steeper slopes but we had spikes so was not a problem
Icy but doable. Pay for parking - someone received a ticket. Came at 10am park full when back at 12pm.
Trail was good - a bit icy but with good boots you were fine. trail right down to the falls was closed but could still get some good views
nice trail, would recommend wearing crampons and/or bringing poles when going down the trail to the falls as it's sloped and slippery with snow and ice.
Great trail with a couple steep hills. Beautiful views. Quite busy on Sunday’s.
Walk to the falls was closed so could only view from half way up.
Good trail. Lots of dog poo on the trail, so watch your step!
a bit busy. the falls are blocked off but still worth the hike
Unique and challenging
Very crowded possibly due to COVID. A good idea to take unconventional route to avoid people. Otherwise a great walk! Need to pay for parking.

I got there around 11am on a Friday and had no issues finding parking. The beginning of the hike was very flat and not super interesting but the vegetation and tree coverage changes every 15 minutes up until you reach the falls (that was pretty unique to observe). You definitely need good shoes since there’s a good balance of incline and decline throughout this hike. This place is a short drive from the gta so I would recommend it for the hike itself rather then the view.

Park fills up fast and the trail gets fairly busy. Access to the water fall is currently closed. Terrain is fairly steep on the out and back the waterfall, the rest is fairly flat. Still a good trail though.

Arrived at 9am and park closed at 10:45am due to maximum capacity so plan early. The trails are mostly fields with some dense forest near the end. The trail was closed at the end leading to the waterfall. Could definitely use some more maintenance.
Great butt workout to the falls. Our 3 yr old made it though. Not an amazing view and busy trail so probably won’t be back.
Semi- casual trail with light incline close to the falls. Washrooms at the beginning and halfway to the falls.
Do this for the hills not a view of the falls. It was hard pack and medium stones on trail, “stairs” on hill section.
It was ok

Bit disappointed. We parked at main lot and hiked all the way in. Many hills up down then up again. Only to be held way back from falls at end point. So far could barely get a good site of it. If you like the challenge of up and down steep hills then this is for you. If you’d rather have a more rewarding reward try another
Not bad

Challenging with lots of inclines.  Make sure to wear proper shoes.  Not a trail for sandals.  If you go straight at the vault toilet, there is a beautiful area by the river.  Not to be missed.  Today was 35 degrees plus humidity.  Take lots of water.

Paid parking. They don’t let anyone in after 4:00 but the park remains open until 8:00pm (don’t quote me on the closing time). A lot of elevation changes and during the weekend it gets busy. The trail by Cataract Falls is closed so you will have to go back the way you came. We will be doing all the trails at the Forks. Go for an ice cream in Belfountain afterwards.  Well worth the stop.

Great ability to see Monarch Butterflies in the milkweed fields.
Waterfall accessible via paths that are rocky, and sandy, and with moderate hill elevations.
Lots of high low incline. Of your going to see the falls,  be aware/caution of the gravel as it tends to break easily.
Beautiful trail, gorgeous scenery and well maintained, it's a shame that someone could throw garbage around a beautiful area but it didn't bother me too much.
This trail is actually enjoyable during the weekdays, not so much the weekends.

This trail was more challenging that I expected. Lots of inclines/declines, some of which were a tad steep and slippery. 
Very much a tourist destination, so go early to avoid the crowds. 
The main waterfall look out was closed, however some hikers must have bent the sign and cut through the barrier so people were able to go through anyways (at their own risk). 
Lots of garbage around the waterfall itself despite the fact that there are garbage cans provided at the beginning and in the middle of the trail. 
The trail itself is a beautiful hike and I completely get why people would want to see it.
I will be doing this hike again, but during the weekdays so there's less traffic.
Peaceful
Hard to get down to the falls and lots of hills but a great hike!

Wonderful trail. Shaded for most part first two kilometres are easy rolling hills. Last stretch is very steep and difficult. Use walking sticks. I would not recommend for children under the age of 8. Waterfall view is not clear - try not to go on the closed bridge it is dangerous. Bathrooms are available in the beginning and middle of trail - clean. No hand wash stations. Parking seems plenty with two lots. Cost is 7.50 for 4 hours 15.50 for whole day. Some trails are closed for bikes and horse riding. Clean trail - it is narrow please use single file and on the right while passing others.
The lookout for the falls is closed (and looks broken). trail is ridiculously crowded (even with the limit on car parking) towards noon. If you like actually hiking, skip it.

One of my favorite trails in the GTA for a workout, your legs & glutes will definitely be sore the next day even if you're an active gym goer. There is free parking available however washrooms are currently closed due to COVID. Another thing I have noticed due to COVID is this trail is 5x as busy as it normally is. I am glad people are getting out and  enjoying nature, however it is not as peaceful of a hike as it use to be.

There are 3 sections of this trail. Section one is a beautiful hilly valley with a nice big lake. I encourage you to venture off the path a bit and  wander through the tall grass near the lake. It is nice to escape from the crowd for a bit and hear the birds chirp and absorb the beauty around you.  Section 2 is the forested area, very beautiful pictures do not do it justice. This area is on a steep incline which is manageable going down but I don't know a single person who isn't huffing and puffing by the time they make their way back up. Bring water for sure and make sure you save some for your journey back up this incline! I also wouldn't recommend strollers unless torturing yourself is your thing. Section 3 is the falls. If you do a little of exploring, you can actually get on top of the falls where there is that famous graffiti structure is located. Best view from this location.

Great trail but the GTA crowd throws their garbage everywhere and that really hurts the ascetic amongst other things. 
Province needs to add lock style garbage bins to help curve this. Rather unfortunate.
Litter seen throughout. Trail was very, very busy, with inconsiderate people playing musical loudly and not sharing the space.

Great trail. Pasture trails to start (no shade), then forested trail down to the falls. Worth the trip down, but prepare yourself for the hike, serious uphill/downhill through the woods. Note: parking is open, but facilities (i.e. bathrooms) are not due to Covid-19.
Nice winter day for a hike, trail was fresh with snow but lots of ice below. Great elevations for getting the pulse up.
Great trail. The wooded portion on way to the falls was the highlight. Elevation on this leg was a fair effort. Very quiet when we first arrived but the lot was full by 11:30 am.

Enjoyed the hike.  Found the signs confusing though (met someone else who did as well)
Moderate due to some good hills ( especially to waterfall)
Recommend and will go back

Great invigorating hike with plenty of uphill and downhill segments. Working your way to the waterfalls makes for a great destinAtion. 

A well travelled path. Not alone too often.
Part of the trail is closed so you can’t get near the falls which was disappointing.

Great hike with some ups and downs through the woods. Well maintained. Currently lookout platform was closed and trail didn‘t loop back. Even if it was open the view of the falls would have been mostly obstructed by trees.
Very beautiful but really muddy
Too damn icy.

Forks of the credit falls trail is my favourite close to Toronto.  More moderate than easy due to the uphill and downhill climbing, but the waterfall at the end is nice and you really forget about the city while you're hiking.
Lots of different walking conditions. Steep in spots but not for to long. Sad the end part of falls viewing is closed. But great hike to falls!
Quite nice !
Great trail, nice and dry this time of year. Some construction going on/clear cutting but it can be avoided.
